precepts.text: Go to Shiloh and see what I did to it; I will cast out Judah as I cast out the whole seed of Ephraim.
precepts.point: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, told Amos to go prophesy in Judah and not in the king's chapel. Amos was sent to his own people, as God always sends prophets to Israel alone.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Amos warns Ephraim, “seek not Beth–el, nor enter into Gilgal”, for “Beth–el shall come to nought.” These were places built for worship by Abraham and Jacob, and Ephraim turned them into seats of idolatry. So Gilgal would surely go into captivity, and Beth–el would be destroyed. “Seek the Lord, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph”: the house of Joseph is Ephraim.

Jeremiah turns the same judgment on Judah: “But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.” Go look at Shiloh and see what I did to it. “I spake unto you, rising up early and speaking, but ye heard not; and I called you, but ye answered not”: they refused the prophets.

“Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh. And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” What was done to Ephraim will be done to Judah: the heathen come in, destroy the sanctuary and lead them captive. The exact same way. The same thing happens to both houses, both kingdoms. He raised up Assyria to overthrow Ephraim, and he raised up Babylon to overthrow Judah.

And they would not hear it. Amaziah the priest of Bethel, one of the low-level priests raised up that was not Levi, told Amos, “go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel”. Go teach Judah; you are disturbing the king's church. Amos was blitzing the churches. But the Lord said to him, “Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.” The Lord always sent his prophets to his people, and his people alone, to repent. It is the same with Jacob today: the one preaching the word of God is called a troublemaker.

So Bethel came to nought as Shiloh did, and Israel went “into captivity forth of his land”: their wives made harlots, their sons and daughters fallen by the sword, their land divided by line as it is to this day, dying “in a polluted land”. That began with the northern kingdom, but eventually it happened to all of us as a whole.

precepts.text: Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded not burnt offerings, but this thing: obey my voice, and I will be your God.
precepts.point: Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and he grew tired of the empty offerings: put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. He spake not unto our fathers concerning burnt offerings, but this thing commanded he: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience; today he does not want an apology or money in the plate, he wants you to obey his voice and repent.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The offerings were the collateral of those times, scaled to what a man could bring, and families felt the after-effects of always sacrificing: the livestock and the agriculture went for your sins, and the household lacked because of it. Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and He grew tired of the empty offerings.

“Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience. Today He does not want an apology or money in the plate; He wants you to obey His voice and repent.

precepts.text: Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded obedience: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people.
precepts.point: Jeremiah carries the same word: I spake not unto your fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices, but this thing commanded I them, obey my voice. Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Jeremiah carries the same word as Hosea: “Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

Yet they hearkened not, but walked in the counsels of their evil heart and went backward and not forward; speak all these words unto them, but they will not hearken. That is seen every sabbath on the streets.

precepts.text: I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: but this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people.
precepts.point: Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord. What he commanded first was obedience: mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression.

precepts.text: Because they built the high places of Topheth to burn their sons and daughters, the Lord said it would be called the valley of slaughter and their carcases would be meat for the fowls.
precepts.point: Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
The Lord says, “they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.”

Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children. It had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own, and Josiah “defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.”

And the Lord said what it would become: “it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place. And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth.”

precepts.text: They built the high places of Tophet in the valley of Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, a thing the Most High commanded not, neither came it into His heart.
precepts.point: He burned incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom and burned his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen that the Most High cast out before the children of Israel. This was witchcraft and child sacrifice, the practice called Tophet, in the high places under every green tree.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

precepts.why:
“For the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, saith the Lord”. “And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.”

That is what Ahaz did. He “burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.” This was witchcraft and child sacrifice, the practice called Tophet, in the high places “and under every green tree.”

Ahaz “did not that which was right in the sight of the Lord, like David his father”. He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and “made also molten images for Baalim”, a thing the Most High commanded not, neither came it into his heart.

precepts.text: The Most High spake not to the fathers concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices when He brought them out of Egypt.
precepts.point: Christ did only what the Most High intended, to make His soul an offering for sin. The scripture always shows that sacrifice was temporary and that obedience and mercy were desired above it.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
The Most High said, “I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices”. Sacrifice was never the heart of what he asked of Israel when he brought them out of Egypt.

That is why setting aside the sacrifice and offerings is not changing the customs Moses delivered, as the false witnesses claimed. The scripture always shows that sacrifice was temporary. It is written throughout the old testament, so Christ destroyed nothing of the law when the sacrifice was set aside.

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

precepts.why: “He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” He says, I know God, I’ve got God in my heart; he is a liar, and the truth is not in him. Israel hearkened not and did worse than their fathers, yet says, I know God: that is a liar.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

precepts.why:
This is what Jeremiah was teaching: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” That throne frames mischief by laws: it allows sin through legality. Through the law you can commit an abortion; it is legal, and certain states say you can do it at two months, three months, four months, five months. Esau says, we’re telling you, you got the right to kill that baby.

So who are you going to follow, God or the white man? God says you are a murderer; that is murder. They try to water the term down and call it abortion. No: it is child sacrifice, the same burning of sons and daughters done at Tophet.

note.label: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

precepts.why:
Truth is perished from their mouth, and Jeremiah 4 shows why: “For my people is foolish, they have not known me.” His people, not everybody in this world, not everybody who so-called loves him: the twelve tribes of the nation of Israel. He is their God and they have not known him.

“They are sottish children”: sottish means stupid, stupefied. They are stupid children, “and they have none understanding.” They do not understand who they are, what happened to them, what is happening to them, what they are supposed to be doing in life, or how they got in this condition.

“They are wise to do evil.” Our people love evil, and love crime, and the other word for crime is sin: fornication, adulteries, robbing, stealing and killing. “But to do good they have no knowledge.” That is why we rise up early and teach them on these street corners, so they will have no excuse in that day, the day they drop dead or the day Christ returns.

It is what the Deacons brought out going over the turbulent 60s: we stood up and fought in the 60s, then in the 70s and 80s we slid right down the hill, the young lion turned old. We have no knowledge how to do good: how to build our communities, work together, stand strong for the Lord, build our families, or teach the young. The older men used to teach the young men and the older women the young girls; now they are hanging with them and competing with each other.

note.label: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

precepts.why:
“Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” We are all supposed to have that same desire Paul had: that all Israel could be saved.

“They have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.” All these gangs, the fraternities, the sororities, the bikers, say they believe in God. They have crosses on their necks, Cesare Borgia on their arms, prayer hands on their arms and on their chains. They think that cross is going to protect them, and that having a Bible in the car is going to help them, without opening it up and reading and applying what it says. God gave us ways out, and they refuse them and run backward, not forward.

“Going about to establish their own righteousness”: you only live once; I got to do what I got to do; I got to feed my kids. They do not think as a community or as a nation; they think as individuals, the way the United States taught us. They “have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God”, they have not submitted to this Bible yet. Some of them are going to change. We are going to show who these so-called gangs are according to the Bible, because God is talking about them.

note.label: | SABBATH MORNING CLASS: When The Harvest Is Ripe

precepts.why:
“Yet they hearkened not unto me, nor inclined their ear, but hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.” This is what we do not want to repeat. We come into this truth and then take it for granted. We go through the motions in this truth when God has given us a second chance unto Christ. We hit and miss on the Sabbath, and we treat our brothers and sisters any type of way.

No, Israel, we are not to be like that, not to be like our forefathers. That is how you harden your neck: acting like this thing ain’t the most important thing in your life. It should be what you think about on the daily. The scripture should be flowing daily, and we should be trying to be here every day if we can.

When we were in wickedness, we took it to a whole other level. So we have to do the same thing coming back to Christ in our repentance.

note.label: Must Be Hated To Be Heard! The Price Of Speaking Truth To Modern Day Christians

precepts.why:
The Christian church literally believes it can do anything it wants and the Lord is pleased with it. This was spoken to our forefathers in their folly, but it is the Christian church today: “Behold, ye trust in lying words, that cannot profit.” Not only this one self-proclaimed pastor; there are many others outside the 2819 Church. The issue is that the people are not studying and holding these pastors accountable. You need to study for yourself so you can figure out what is right and what is wrong.

“Will ye steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not; And come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, We are delivered to do all these abominations?” That is what the Christian church does: they keep no laws and tell you God is okay with it. That is what you are saying when you say the law is done away with. They say the law is fulfilled, but they do not understand grammar: if you fulfill the law, you do it, you keep it.

That is called, I am under grace. But think of a grace period on a light bill: it is given so you end up paying it, not so you keep on being delinquent.

Verse three: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.” To amend is to change and to fix. The Lord wants us to change.

points: “I have even sent unto you all my servants the prophets, daily rising up early.” He sends us out to the streets early, crying with the scriptures in the chief places of concourse to wake the people up and bring them back to him. He sends us into dangerous places and dangerous territories, and we go and do the work of the Lord. We are not trying to wake up everybody; we are looking for his chosen, the needle out of the haystack.

note.label: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

points: “Yet they hearkened not.” We come to their corners and their neighborhoods and they still do not want to listen to the Lord. They “hardened their neck: they did worse than their fathers.” We are worse than our fathers now, worshipping more gods and more deities than our fathers did.

When we say gangbangers, it is not just red and blue. The fraternities, the sororities, the motorcycle gangs, the car clubs: they are all gangs. The police department, the COs, the Department of Corrections: they are gangs too.

note.label: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

points: “Thou shalt speak all these words unto them.” We go and tell them what the Lord said, “but they will not hearken.” “Thou shalt also call unto them”: we call them daily, through the fire missions, through youth violence programs, community cleanups, libraries, prisons and hospitals, two by two on the street corners, telling them to return and come back to the Father. “But they will not answer thee.”

note.label: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

points: “This is a nation that obeyeth not the voice of the Lord their God, nor receiveth correction.” They do not want to receive the correction we give them; they do not want to accept the rebuke handed to them. “Truth is perished, and is cut off from their mouth.”

note.label: From Gangbangers To Saviors Of Our Nation

points: Jeremiah is prophesying against Judah. “Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust”: this house is referring to the southern kingdom; it’s referring to the temple. “And unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh.” Shiloh is the northern kingdom. So what I am going to do to this house, the southern kingdom, the temple here, is the same thing I did to Shiloh. What the Lord says he did to the northern kingdom he is now going to do to the southern kingdom.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: “And I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” I cast all of them out; I’m going to cast all of you out. The same thing he said he would do to Judah, he already did to Ephraim. What he did to Ephraim with Assyria, he would do to Judah with Babylon.

note.label: Gentiles: What Happened to Northern Kingdom?

points: “Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name, wherein ye trust, and unto the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh.” This is the Lord prophesying against the southern kingdom. Judah followed behind Ephraim into idolatry, so the Lord said, what I did to the northern kingdom I am going to do to you. This place is Judea, and Shiloh was the northern kingdom’s capital, the first place of worship.

note.label: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: “I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim.” He will cast Judah, the southern kingdom, out of his sight, as he cast out their brethren, the northern kingdom.

The Lord sent Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians against the southern kingdom, and he did the exact same thing Shalmaneser did to the northern kingdom: but Nebuchadnezzar left behind a remnant of the southern kingdom, the poor, in the land. In the same way, the Assyrian king left behind a remnant of the northern kingdom in their land. The same thing happened to both kingdoms by different nations: the Assyrians conquered the northern kingdom, the Babylonians conquered the southern kingdom, and both left remnants in the land.

note.label: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: This scripture goes with Diana and with 1 Corinthians 14, the women being told to keep silence. “The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven”: y’all see that, what they’re doing, making cakes to the queen of heaven, the mother goddess.

So don’t think that feminism just started. Feminism is just a new name; its essence was way back in the past. “And to pour out drink offerings unto other gods, that they may provoke me to anger”: that worship of the woman provokes God to anger.
